It affects Axios versions 1.7.0 through 1.19.x (fixed in 1.20.0) when the fetch adapter is used in Node.js environments. The vulnerability was disclosed on September 16, 2026, and published to NVD on September 28, 2026. It carries a CVSS v4.0 base score of 6.9 (Medium) (GitHub Advisory, Red Hat Bugzilla). Technical details The root cause is a logic flaw (CWE-628: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments) combined with a prototype pollution gadget (CWE-1321). In lib/adapters/fetch.js, Axios builds a resolvedOptions object with sanitized headers and constructs a Request object from it, but then calls _fetch(request, fetchOptions) — passing the original, unsanitized fetchOptions as the second argument instead of resolvedOptions. In Node.js runtimes backed by undici, the second argument to fetch() can override headers already set on the Request object. If a separate prototype-pollution vulnerability in the same process has set Object.prototype.headers to attacker-controlled values, fetchOptions.headers resolves through prototype inheritance and overrides the sanitized headers. The fix in PR #11141 creates a null-prototype copy of fetchOptions (safeFetchOptions), strips Axios-managed fields (headers, method, body, signal, duplex, credentials) from it, and passes this safe copy as the second argument (GitHub Advisory, Fix Commit). Impact Successful exploitation allows an attacker to inject arbitrary HTTP headers — including Authorization, Cache-Control, and cloud metadata service access headers — into outbound requests made by the vulnerable Axios fetch adapter, while simultaneously suppressing legitimate caller-specified headers. This can lead to authorization bypass, cache poisoning, unauthorized access to cloud instance metadata services (e.g., AWS IMDSv1), or manipulation of application-specific header-based security controls. The vulnerability does not affect confidentiality or availability of the vulnerable system directly, but poses a high integrity risk to subsequent systems receiving the manipulated requests (GitHub Advisory, Feedly). It provides a simple API for sending asynchronous requests to REST endpoints and handling responses. The library is widely used in both client-side and server-side applications due to its ease of use and flexibility. However, a vulnerability has been identified in the fetch adapter of Axios, which can lead to unauthorized modification of outbound requests due to prototype pollution. Vulnerability Detail The vulnerability arises from the way Axios handles fetch options in its fetch adapter. Specifically, when making requests, Axios merges user-defined fetch options with inherited properties from Object.prototype. This can allow an attacker, who has previously exploited a prototype pollution vulnerability elsewhere in the application, to manipulate the headers of outgoing requests. As a result, sensitive headers can be overridden, potentially affecting authorization, cache behavior, and other critical application functionalities. The issue is specific to the fetch adapter and does not impact the Node HTTP adapter. Scan free → Workaround If you cannot immediately update Axios, consider using the Node HTTP adapter for server-side requests. Additionally, avoid passing empty fetchOptions objects in environments where prototype pollution may occur. Basic Information for CVE-2026-101908 AIGC Shenlong Model CVE Program / CVE List V5 Vulnerability Information Axios: Prototype pollution gadget in fetch adapter can alter outbound requests Overview A prototype pollution vulnerability exists in Axios versions 1.7.0 to 1.20.0. This vulnerability occurs because the fetch adapter uses sanitized resolvedOptions when constructing a Request object, but uses the original fetchOptions when actually invoking fetch. Due to prototype pollution within the same process, Object.prototype.headers is populated with malicious values. Consequently, fetchOptions.headers inherits these maliciously controlled values through the prototype chain, thereby overwriting the previously sanitized Request headers. Affected Versions Affected versions: 1.7.0 to 1.20.0 Fixed version: 1.20.0 Details Vulnerability Mechanism: The code first constructs a Request object based on sanitized options, but then passes un sanitized original fetchOptions when calling the fetch function. Exploitation Conditions: There must be another path or code within the same process that causes Object.prototype.headers to be polluted, allowing fetchOptions to inherit the malicious headers attribute.
